HOW TO READ THIS PAGE

Status means what you can do today.

Each feature has exactly one status for the audited game version. Creative and survival differences are noted on the feature. A planned feature is never described as playable here, even when work on it has started.

Available 140
In the normal game. No pack, developer build or command-line option is needed.
Limited 14
Playable now, with limits that the game itself documents. The limits are listed on the feature.
Developer tool 6
For testing and debugging: command-line options, developer builds or diagnostic exports.
In development 3
Some code exists, but ordinary players cannot use it yet.
Planned 24
Requested and tracked, but absent from the audited game version. No guide is written until it ships.

AREA 01 OF 12

Starting out: menus, modes & saving

The start menu, worlds, creative and survival, pausing, saving and quitting.

Creative and survival modes (F4)

Available

Creative · Survival

There are exactly two modes. Press F4 any time to switch between creative and survival; your pack, hotbar and position stay as they are. New worlds always start in creative, and each world remembers the mode it was saved in.

F4
Switch creative / survival (in the world (refused while connected to a server))

Creative: instant breaking and free placing, free crafting, any tool and unlimited ammunition, the Build tab and catalog, building brushes and undo, middle-click block picking, flight, map travel and teleport, editable time/weather/season, one-hit animal removal without drops. Survival: timed mining with tool advice, carry capacity, health/hunger/thirst/stamina/temperature with HUD bars, fall damage, R eat / T drink / X quick craft, World tab read-only, respawn at your rest point. No hardcore, peaceful or difficulty settings exist (grep found none).

Start menu

Available

Menus

The start menu offers Continue and Worlds for opening worlds, plus Settings, Credits, Study timer and Quit, with the current world's name shown above the buttons. Use the mouse or the Up/Down arrows and Enter; Esc returns from any sub-page.

Enter or click
Open the selected entry (start menu)
Esc
Return to the first page (start-menu sub-page)
P
Open Study Grove (start menu, not typing on the Worlds page)

The first launch shows a tumbling wireframe-cube loading animation; later world loads show only the stage text and an activity bar. The source audit read the menu background as a dark fill with the cube mark; a headless capture of the audited build shows the menu panel drawn over a lit world scene with the cube, so the background of a real window is unconfirmed.

Worlds: create, load, search and delete

Available

Menus

Worlds lists your saves, current world first, then alphabetically. Type to filter the list or to name a new world, then choose Create world. Click a row or press Enter to load it. To delete a world, hold its DELETE badge or the Delete key for 3 seconds; the current world cannot be deleted.

Typing
Filter the list / name the next new world (Worlds page)
Backspace / Ctrl+Backspace
Delete one character / clear the field (Worlds page)
Up / Down arrows
Move through worlds, Create world and Back (Worlds page)
Enter or click a row
Load that world (Worlds page)
Enter or click Create world
Create and enter a new world (Worlds page)
Hold Delete (row selected) or hold the DELETE badge
Delete that world after 3 s (Worlds page, not the current world)
Esc or Back
Return to the start menu (Worlds page)

There is no seed, mode or option picker: new worlds always start in creative. Only four rows show and the mouse wheel does not scroll this list, so use the arrows or type to filter. No rename, backup, favourites or thumbnails yet (planned).

Settings menu basics

Available

Any mode

Press Esc in the world to open Settings; the game pauses and the panel is titled 'Paused'. Switch between the General, Audio, World and Debug tabs with the mouse or Tab/Shift+Tab, pick chips or drag sliders, or use the arrow keys. Resume, Main menu and Save & quit are at the bottom.

Esc
Open Settings / close it again (in the world)
Tab / Shift+Tab
Next / previous tab (Settings)
Up / Down arrows
Select a row (Settings)
Left / Right arrows (Enter = Right)
Change the selected value (Settings)
Click a chip / drag a slider
Set a value directly (Settings)
Right click a row
Step that value backward (Settings)
Resume / Main menu / Save & quit
Return to play / save and go to the start menu / save and exit (in-game Settings)
Back
Return to the start menu (start-menu Settings)

Settings live inside each world's save, so loading another world brings back that world's settings, and Create world copies the current ones. Hover a row label for a tooltip. Right-click stepping is undocumented.

Esc key and what pauses the game

Available

Any mode

Esc closes whatever is open (pack panel, large map, Study Grove, a start-menu sub-page) and recaptures the mouse; with nothing open it opens Settings and frees the mouse. Settings, the large map, the start menu and Study Grove pause the world; the pack panel does not.

Esc
Close the open layer, or open Settings (anywhere)

Esc closes the whole pack panel even while typing in its search box (use Enter to leave a search field).

Mouse capture and release

Available

Any mode

Click the world to capture the mouse; that click never mines or places. Opening a panel, Esc, Print Screen, losing focus or being covered releases it, and it is not recaptured when focus returns. While released you cannot move or look.

Click the world
Capture the mouse (click is not used in game) (pointer released, no panel open)
Print Screen
Release the mouse for a system screenshot tool (anywhere)
Esc
Open Settings and release the mouse (in the world)

Print Screen does not take a screenshot itself; the game has no screenshot key. If the system refuses the pointer grab, controls stay released with a message.

Saving, Main menu and quitting

Available

Any mode

The world autosaves about every 30 seconds when it has unsaved changes, and F6 saves at once ('World saved safely'). Settings > Main menu saves and returns to the start menu. Ctrl+Q, Save & quit, Quit or closing the window all save first; if saving fails, the game stays open.

F6

Ctrl+Q

Window, fullscreen and title

Available

Any mode

F11 or Alt+Enter toggles borderless fullscreen. The window opens at 1280x720 and cannot shrink below 800x450. Its title shows loading stages, 'Main Menu', 'Paused / Settings', the latest status message, or a detailed FPS/position line while FPS and coordinates is on. Launching again just focuses the open game.

F11 or Alt+Enter
Toggle borderless fullscreen (anywhere)

Fullscreen is not remembered between launches (no saved window state found). The owner plans a plain 'voxelgame' title and keeping the display awake; neither is present.

Keyboard, mouse and controller support

Limited

Any mode

The game is played with keyboard and mouse only: there is no gamepad support and keys cannot be rebound. Keys are read by physical position, so on non-QWERTY keyboards use the keys where W A S D sit on a QWERTY board.

Known Linux issue: an active Pinyin input method on X11 can swallow movement keys (unresolved). Because key repeat is ignored, holding Backspace deletes one character; Ctrl+Backspace clears the Worlds search and map coordinate fields. Non-ASCII characters are dropped from names and searches (chat accepts printable ASCII). Known issue: on X11, a Pinyin input method can swallow movement keys; a reliable fix is not verified yet (game TODO.md).

Moving, camera & screen

Walking, jumping, sneaking, crawling, swimming and flying, the camera, and what the screen shows you.

Walking and looking around

Available

Creative · Survival

Move with W A S D and look with the mouse once the pointer is captured. You walk at about 4.3 m/s, climb half-metre steps without jumping, and need to jump onto a full one-metre block.

W / A / S / D
Walk forward / left / back / right (on foot, pointer captured)
Mouse
Look around (pointer captured, no panel open)

Keys are physical positions: on AZERTY or other layouts use the key that sits where W is on a QWERTY board. Jumps mostly keep their take-off direction. Movement runs on a fixed 60 Hz tick, so speed does not depend on frame rate.

Sprinting

Available

Creative · Survival

Hold Ctrl while moving forward with W to sprint at about 5.6 m/s. A sprint-jump adds a small forward push. In survival, sprinting uses stamina and stops when stamina is nearly empty.

Ctrl + W (hold)
Sprint (on foot, not sneaking or crawling)
Ctrl + Space while sprinting
Sprint-jump with a small forward push (on foot)

Ctrl with only A, D or S held does not sprint. High speed also widens the view slightly (see camera-bob-and-speed-fov).

Creative · Survival

Swimming and diving

Available

Creative · Survival

Once water reaches your chest you swim. W and S follow the direction you look (look down to dive), Space swims up, Shift dives and Ctrl swims faster; with no keys you hold your depth.

Space (hold)

Shift (hold)
Dive (in water)
Ctrl + W (hold)

Ankle-deep wading stays upright. No drowning or air meter was found in this code (grep drown/breath/oxygen); being underwater only drains stamina slowly in survival.

Camera bob and speed field of view

Available

Creative · Survival

Walking gently bobs the camera; turn it off in Settings > General > Camera bob. Moving fast widens the view by up to 5 degrees beyond your field-of-view setting, and there is no option to turn that widening off.

Because the widening reads total velocity, jumps and falls also change the field of view, not only sprinting. No reduced-motion or comfort option exists; owner fixes are planned (VOX-OWNER-SPRINT-JUMP-FOV). There is no camera bob when taking damage (VOX-OWNER-DAMAGE-BOB is planned).

Crosshair and aiming reticle

Available

Creative · Survival

A small plus-shaped crosshair marks your aim and turns green-tinted when a block is in reach. With a bow, rifle or throwable it becomes a ring of dots whose size shows your current inaccuracy, shifting from orange to green as your aim steadies.

A four-line crosshair whose gap shows spread (with colour inversion) is planned to replace the ring.

Available

Survival shows four bars: HP, HUNGER, THIRST and STAMINA (0-100). A full hunger bar lasts about 40 minutes and a full thirst bar about 30 minutes; health slowly regenerates while both stay above 65.

Body temperature and shelter

Available

Survival

Your body temperature drifts toward the air temperature and costs health only outside -12 to 48 C. Air temperature depends on time of day, season, rain and altitude (not biome); a roof and walls pull it toward 20 C.

With these numbers heat damage cannot happen (air peaks around 32 C) and cold damage needs very high altitude (roughly 600 m up on a rainy winter night, more otherwise). Body temperature itself is never displayed. Hot blocks such as Magma stone or Boiling water do not hurt.

Fall damage and other dangers

Available

Survival

Falls of up to 3 m are free; each extra metre costs 5 HP, so about 23 m is fatal from full health. Animals never attack; besides falls, only starvation, thirst, extreme cold and explosions hurt you.

No drowning, lava, fire, cactus or hostile-mob damage exists in this snapshot. Fall damage only applies when landing on solid ground.

Death and respawn

Available

Survival

At 0 HP you respawn immediately at your rest point (the world start point until you rest at home) and lose nothing: pack, hotbar and home storage stay as they were.

The default rest point is where the world started. Establishing a home does not move it; only Rest does. When connected to a server, the client does not apply death (multiplayer is in development).

Home crate: establish, storage, repair, pack up

Available

Creative · Survival

In the Home tab, Establish home while standing on dry, solid ground: it costs 8 board pieces (free in creative) and places a small crate 1.5 m beside you. The crate stores up to 400 kg while you are within 6 m.

Click Establish home
Place the crate (or repair a lost one at its original spot) (Home tab)
Click a carried / stored row
Move one item into / out of storage (Home tab, within 6 m of the crate)
Shift+click a row
Move as many as fit (Home tab)
Click Pack up
Remove the crate; survival refunds 8 Alder boards (Home tab, storage empty)

One home at a time; to move it, empty storage and Pack up. If the crate is destroyed (e.g. by TNT) the stored items are kept and Establish home within 6 m of the old spot repairs it. Pack up refunds Alder boards even if you paid with other species. Your rest point stays after packing up.

Resting and setting your respawn point

Available

Creative · Survival

Home tab > Rest / set respawn works within 6 m of your crate, on dry ground, under a roof with cover on at least two sides. It sets your respawn point there and refills stamina, but does not heal or feed you.

Leaves and tree trunks count as solid cover; plants and water do not. The shelter check runs when you press Rest; its temperature effect is re-checked every 0.5 s.

Carry capacity (mass-based pack)

Available

Creative · Survival

Your pack is limited by total weight, not slots: 80 kg, with no stack limit. Blocks are carried as half-metre pieces; a full 1 m block is 8 pieces and weighs what the block weighs.

The same 80 kg pack is used in creative: taking catalog items is capacity-limited, but creative block placement does not use up items. The owner-requested capacity of 1000 is planned, not implemented.

Ten-slot hotbar

Available

Creative · Survival

The hotbar has ten slots that you bind to item kinds; they start empty. Bind by hovering an item and pressing a number key, or by dragging; select slots with 1-9 and 0, the mouse wheel, or [ and ].

Mouse wheel / [ ]
Cycle hotbar slots (on foot, inventory closed)
Hover item + 1-9/0

Drag item onto slot
Bind it; drag slot onto slot swaps; drag a slot off the bar clears it (inventory open)
Click an empty slot
Select it (inventory open)

Slots are bindings, not containers: the count is everything of that kind in the pack. Bindings are saved with the world. Selecting a block slot puts away any tool, since an equipped tool blocks placement. With an empty slot selected the label reads 'EMPTY HANDS | E OPEN INVENTORY'.

Interchangeable ingredients

Available

Creative · Survival

Some ingredients accept a group of materials you can mix: boards of any species, any of 26 natural stones, any hardwood log or deadwood, and plant fiber or wool. Every other ingredient must be that exact material.

Exact-only ingredients include Pale sand (not other sands), River clay (not ochre/umber/sienna/cracked/banded clay), Reeds (not Tall reeds), Limestone (plaster), Granite (polish), Natural cobble and Moss (mossy cobble), Chalk, Basalt, Red ironstone, Glass, Feather, Raw meat, Venison, Lumen crystal. Not usable as natural stone: Magma stone, Iron ore chunks, Bog iron, Amethyst, Salt, Sulfur crust, Mineral crust, Geyserite and all crafted masonry. Mixed species keep their own identity in the pack until spent.

Mining speed and tool effectiveness

Available

Survival

Any block can be mined by hand; a tool only speeds up its own material class. Pickaxe x4 on rock, crystal, glass, ice and masonry; hatchet x3.6 on logs, boards, leaves and other wooden blocks; shovel x3.4 on loose ground.

The time is for the whole targeted 1 m block; detail (Shift) mining takes the same time for one piece. Petal carpet and Leaf litter are plants that a shovel speeds up; Bamboo and Date clusters are plants a hatchet speeds up.

Felling trees

Available

Creative · Survival

Cutting a log on a natural tree (or a cactus) brings down that piece and everything growing from it. In survival the chop takes the combined time of all removed wood and leaves, and all of it goes into your pack.

Cutting the root removes the whole tree; cutting a branch keeps the trunk below. If the whole harvest does not fit you get 'Need X kg free to collect this connected tree' and nothing is cut. Logs you placed yourself mine like ordinary blocks. Status shows 'Felled a tree: N <log> and M <leaves>'.

Available

Where crafting materials come from

Available

Survival

Natural stone and wood are everywhere; Pale sand and River clay line shores, Reeds grow in wetlands, Wild flax (for fiber) grows in meadows of new worlds, and feathers, wool and meat come from animals.

Biome placement detail belongs to the world audit; this list only links recipe inputs to known sources. Older (generation-9) worlds have no Wild flax, so use Wool for bindings there. Lumen crystal has no practical survival source (see lumen-crystal-supply).

Block types and material families

Available

Creative · Survival

Placing blocks

Available

Creative · Survival

Select a block and right click to place a full 1 m cube (eight half-metre pieces) in the cell beside the face you aim at. Creative placement is free; in survival each whole block spends 8 carried pieces of that material.

Place the held block at the ghost (one block per click) (block selected, no tool equipped)

If any part of the 1 m cell is occupied the whole block is refused (red outline); hold Shift to place half-metre pieces instead. Explosions: reach, damage and terrain

Available

Creative · Survival

One whole TNT block blasts about 4.25 m; touching groups explode as one bigger blast (up to 10.5 m), while a single half-metre charge or dynamite stick reaches only about 1.5 m. Survival players near a blast lose health and are knocked back (creative players are unharmed), creatures are hurt in both modes, and blasted blocks are destroyed, not collected.

Derived from the formulas: one whole TNT block cannot break obsidian (strength at most 4.25 + 0.55 < 5.0), and solid rock gives way only close to the charge. Values marked 'about' are computed from code constants, not measured in play. The cleared count in the status line is in half-metre voxels. Explosions are not undoable.

World, weather & landmarks

Generations, biomes, islands, caves, landmarks, expedition sites, time, weather and seasons.

World generations (terrain rule versions)

Available

Any mode

Each world keeps the terrain rules it was created with. Worlds made with Create world use generation 10; older saves keep their older generation, so game updates never reshape existing builds. To see newer terrain, create a new world.

No screen shows the generation number. The only in-game hint is the Journal's expedition section, which says 'Landmarks appear in new generation-10 worlds' when the world is older. Generation-1 worlds cannot contain meteor fields, surface lava tubes or amethyst gorges.

World seeds (players cannot choose one)

Developer tool

Menus

Create world asks only for a name and picks a random seed from the clock. You cannot enter or view a seed. The default first world always uses the same fixed meadow-island seed, so every player's default world has the same terrain. Only the developer debug session can set a seed.

92 biomes

Available

Any mode

Worlds contain 92 named biomes, from meadows, orchards and bamboo thickets to salt flats, kelp forests, meteor fields and surface lava tubes. All 92 can generate naturally, and the map locator can find any of them.

You can read your current biome on the FPS-and-coordinates readout (see position-readout) or in the status message after map travel.

Endless archipelago and the starting island

Available

Any mode

The world is an endless sea of island groups. You start at X 0, Z 0 on a large island several kilometres across, in a protected, gentle meadow clearing. Other islands range from small islets and palm-ringed atolls to large islands and occasional continent-sized landmasses. Open ocean separates island groups, and satellite islets sit at least 240 m offshore.

The size figures are internal envelope values, not measured coastline lengths, so the wiki should say only 'several kilometres across'. The starting island keeps its size in every generation (archipelago.rs:159-163). Coordinates: north is -Z, south is +Z and east is +X.

Hillside caves

Available

Any mode

Some hills have cave entrances that lead into one of three layouts: branching passages around a chamber, a looping gallery around a central rock mass, or a broad vaulted hall held up by four rock pillars. Floors climb in walkable half-metre steps. Caves are single, bounded sites rather than deep cave networks.

Caves do not appear on the map. There are no stalactites, dripstone, ores or lights inside caves.

Landmarks: meteor craters, amethyst gorges, lava tubes and other geological…

Available

Any mode

Rare large sites appear across the world. Impact fields have a main crater bowl with a raised ejecta rim plus two smaller craters. Amethyst gorges are winding canyons through crystal-studded rock. On volcanic islands, cooled lava tubes are walkable roofed passages with two open skylights. Other sites include hot-spring terraces, geyser basins, oases, tepui mesas, ice spires, granite domes, karst towers, moraines and limestone pavements.

Meteor craters appear only where the site is not volcanic. Lava tubes appear only on volcanic ground. Generation-1 worlds have no impact, gorge or lava-tube sites.

Volcanoes and volcanic terrain

Available

Any mode

Some islands carry shield volcanoes, steep stratovolcanoes or breached calderas. Older ones are eroded and overgrown. Volcanic ground has basalt, obsidian, ash, lava rock, pahoehoe and glowing magma stone, and nearby geothermal areas have warm and boiling pools and steam vents. Everything is solid and cooled: there is no molten lava, and nothing burns.

No code damages players from magma stone, boiling water or steam vents (grep for MAGMA_STONE/BOILING_WATER/STEAM_VENT outside generation and rendering finds no gameplay use). Steam vents are static blocks with no steam particles.

Available

Any mode

Islands have river channels, inland lakes up to 62 m above sea level, marshes, bogs, mangroves, bayous and frozen lakes. All natural water is still: rivers do not flow or push you. The kind of water depends on the place: ocean water, fresh water in lakes and rivers, black water in warm wetlands, warm or boiling mineral water at hot springs, dark fjord water, and ice on frozen lakes.

Expedition sites and one-time supply finds

Available

Creative · Survival

Generation-10 worlds have three small landmarks within about 300 m of spawn: the Survey workshop to the east, the Reed refuge to the south-west and the Stone overlook to the north-east. Click one in the Journal to make it your destination. Walk to within 12 m of it on foot to discover it, then press Find in the Journal while still nearby to collect its one-time supplies.

Click a site name
Make it your destination (map marker, light beacon and on-screen marker) (Journal)
Find button
Collect the site's supplies; it shows 'Taken' afterwards (Journal, within 12 m of a discovered site, on foot)

If no dry, level spot is found near a site's base position, that site is skipped, so a world can have fewer than three. The site buildings are regenerated each session and do not show on the map, but any blocks you mine or place there are kept. Without enough pack space the game says 'Leave pack space; the find will wait here'. You can still harvest the site's blocks after taking the find. The Reed refuge has a small fresh-water pool, the workshop has a glass block and carved-stone floor, and the overlook has a Lumen crystal light (exploration.rs:192-242).

Day and night

Available

Creative · Survival

A full day and night lasts 20 real minutes: the sun is up for about 10 minutes and down for about 10. New worlds start just after sunrise. Night is darker with cool lighting and a moon, but nothing dangerous happens at night, and there is no way to sleep or skip it. Time of day is saved with the world.

In survival, time of day also changes the air temperature by up to 9 degrees (see seasons). The world clock stops while the fullscreen map or Settings is open.

Automatic weather

Available

Creative · Survival

Weather moves through a fixed 30-minute pattern: clear, cloudy, rain, cloudy, partly cloudy, foggy, cloudy, rainstorm, thunderstorm, cloudy, about 3 minutes each, blending smoothly. Each world starts at a different point in the pattern. Weather is the same everywhere in a world, so rain also falls over deserts and there is no snowfall. Rain stops at roofs, thunderstorms flash with lightning and delayed thunder, and lightning causes no damage or fires.

Weather changes sailing wind strength. In survival, rain lowers the air temperature by up to 2 degrees.

Available

Creative

In creative, press Esc and open Settings > World to set Time of day (Cycle, Dawn, Day, Dusk, Night), Weather (Auto, Clear, Partly, Cloudy, Rain, Storm, Thunder, Foggy) and Season (Auto, Spring, Summer, Autumn, Winter). In survival these rows only display the current state.

Seasons

Limited

Creative · Survival

A year is 80 real minutes, about 20 minutes per season, and new worlds start in summer. Seasons tint grass, deciduous leaves, needles, blossoms, water, sky and sunlight, for example russet autumn foliage and a cooler winter light. Leaves never thin out and nothing turns snowy. In survival, seasons also shift the air temperature, from +7 degrees in summer to -7 in winter, so they are not purely visual yet.

In practice the season changes only the temperature number at normal heights, since sea-level air stays between about 2.5 and 32 degrees. The wiki should describe seasons as mainly visual, with a small survival temperature effect that the owner plans to remove, and must not claim that leaves thin or grass turns snowy.

The compact and fullscreen maps, the locator, journal places, markers and creative travel.

Compact map

Available

Creative · Survival

A small north-up terrain map sits in the top-right corner and is on by default. It shows 128 m around you with your heading arrow, saved places, your destination and any locator highlight. Press M to hide or show it.

M
Show or hide the compact map (in the world)

The terrain moves in 4 m jumps because the view snaps to the sample spacing (map.rs:126-134). Like the fullscreen map, it shows only generated terrain: your builds and dug or blasted ground do not appear.

Available

Creative · Survival

Shift+M opens a north-up world map, 512 m across by default. The mouse wheel zooms from 128 m to about 131 km across, and dragging looks around without moving you. Map locator: find biomes and landmarks

Available

Creative · Survival

The panel left of the fullscreen map lists Volcano, Cliff island and Mountain range, then all 92 biomes alphabetically. Type to filter the list, then click a result or press Enter. The search spirals outward from the map centre, recentres and zooms the map on the first match, highlights matching terrain in cyan and drops a pin with distance and coordinates. It never moves you.

Click the search field and type
Filter places by name or alias (e.g. crystal, meteorite, caldera, lava tunnel) (fullscreen map)
Enter
Search for an exact name match, otherwise the first entry on the current page (search field focused)
Click a list entry
Start searching for that place (fullscreen map)
Mouse wheel over the list, or PREV/NEXT
Change list page (fullscreen map)
FIND NEXT
Continue outward to a match more than about 1 km from the last one (after a match)
CLEAR
Remove the search, pin and cyan highlight (fullscreen map)

The search starts from the map centre, not from you, so pan the map first to search somewhere else. In survival the locator still reveals everything, because there is no fog of war. The highlight and pin stay on the compact map until you press Clear.

Water & sailing

Flowing water, splashes and the small sailing boat.

Launching and packing up a sailing boat

Available

Creative · Survival

Select the Small sailing boat and right-click open water within 6 m to launch it. It floats on any water: sea, lakes and all six water types, at their real surface height. To carry it again, look at an unoccupied boat within 6 m and Shift-right-click, with 18 kg of free carrying capacity. Survival uses up and returns the boat item; creative launches from the catalog without using one.

Right-click open water
Launch the selected boat (Small sailing boat selected, water within 6 m)
Shift + right-click
Pack up the boat you are looking at (unoccupied boat within 6 m, any item held)

A failed launch says 'Boat needs clear water and room for its hull and mast (8 boats maximum)' and uses nothing. Wrecked boats (0 HP) cannot be boarded or packed and are cleared when you next launch (vehicle/sailing.rs:125-141). Boats are disabled on multiplayer servers ('Boats aren't available on servers yet', game/sailing.rs:49). The recipe belongs to the survival audit and is listed here only for reference.

Sailing: deck, helm, sails, steering and camera

Available

Creative · Survival

Walk or jump onto the boat's wooden deck like normal ground. Press V within 9 m to take the helm, and press V again to step back onto the cockpit. At the helm, hold W to raise the sails and S to reef them, press Space to lower them fully, and steer with A/D. Press C or F5 to switch between first-person and chase view, and hold Alt for free look.

V
Take or leave the helm (within 9 m of the boat or on its deck)
W (hold)
Raise the sail setting; the sails follow over about 2 s (at the helm)
S (hold)
Reef (lower the sail setting) (at the helm)
Space
Lower the sails completely (at the helm)
A / D
Steer left / right (rudder eases in and recentres) (at the helm)
C or F5
Switch first-person / chase camera (at the helm)
Hold Alt
Free look (at the helm)

There is no reverse. The boat can turn while stopped. It stops dead if the hull would run aground or hit another boat, and it can only turn where the new heading still has water under the whole hull (vehicle/sailing.rs:159-205), so a grounded boat may need packing up and relaunching. Leaving the helm stops the boat immediately. Opening the pack (E) pauses the boat (game.rs:1149).

Sailing: wind, speed and tacking

Available

Creative · Survival

Each world has a fixed prevailing wind direction, and its strength changes with the weather: about 2.8 m/s in clear weather up to 8.5 m/s in thunderstorms. Running with the wind is fastest, and across the wind gives about two-thirds of the wind speed. Within 45 degrees of sailing straight into the wind the sails give no push, so zig-zag (tack) to go upwind. The red masthead pennant and the HUD flag (bow at the top) point downwind.

Because the wind direction never changes in a world, the same routes are always upwind. The HUD bearing 'TO n DEG' is not a compass bearing: 0 deg points to +Z (south on the map) and 90 deg to +X (east) (vehicle_ui.rs:112). Read the flags instead. Seasons do not affect the wind.

Flowing water (placing and blocking water)

Limited

Creative

In creative, the catalog's Water block is a flowing source: it spreads up to 7 half-metre cells sideways and pours down over edges. Any block placed into water displaces it, and digging next to the sea or a lake lets water flow into the gap. Flowing water never recedes. There are no buckets, survival players cannot pick up or place water, and the other five water types are still blocks that do not flow.

Right-click with Water selected
Place a flowing water source (creative)
Right-click with any block aimed into water
Replace that water cell with the block (building)

To get rid of unwanted flowing water, fill each wet cell with blocks. Water from creative building brushes behaves the same way. On a multiplayer server the server runs the water.

Animal drops

Available

Survival

In survival, an animal you kill puts its drops straight into your pack. Meat and venison are food, feathers make arrows, and wool can replace plant fiber; hide currently has no use.

Drops that do not fit are lost (there are no ground items). Killing animals in creative collects nothing. Hunting controls are covered by the combat audit.

Where and how many animals appear

Available

Creative · Survival

Animals appear around you according to the biome: each biome has its own small group of species and every one of the 94 can appear somewhere; swans turn up in wetlands and deltas, fish only in deep enough water. Up to 36 wild animals are around you at once, with per-species limits; animals more than 180 m away are removed and new ones appear as you explore. Animals are not saved.

Animals do not spawn on built roofs or manufactured floors, and spawning waits while you fly high above the ground.

Animal behaviour

Available

Any mode

Farm animals stay calm near you; shy wild species (rabbits, foxes, frogs, many birds, horses, zebras, giraffes, big cats, wolves, crocodiles and others) keep about 5 m away (frogs 3 m) and run if you come closer. Any hurt animal bolts for a few seconds. Many animals pause to graze and idle animals turn their heads to watch you. Deer, rabbits, frogs, kangaroos and jerboas bound while fleeing; goats, deer and gazelles jump ledges up to 1 m; otters, penguins and swans swim and fish stay in water.

There is no taming, riding, breeding, feeding, milking or shearing (see animal-taming-breeding).

Shader quality: None, Fast, Cinematic

Available

Any mode

Settings > General > Shader picks the lighting tier. None is plain voxel lighting for weak hardware; Fast (default) adds sun shadows, sun rays and haze; Cinematic refines shadows and rays and adds reflective water at extra GPU cost.

Cinematic costs frame time rather than extra memory (settings.rs:160-165). Saved with the world.

Horizon distance

Available

Any mode

Settings > General > Horizon distance sets how far low-detail distant terrain reaches: 8, 16, 32, 48, 64 (default), 96, 128, 192, 256 or 512 chunks. A chunk is 16 m, so 512 reaches about 8 km. The setting's tooltip notes that nearby full-detail blocks stay at nine chunks.

Large horizons are expensive: an offscreen Intel Iris Xe test measured about 1.8-1.9 GiB of distant-terrain vertex buffers and roughly 37-39 ms world GPU passes at 256-512 chunks. A 1024-chunk option is planned, not present.

Install, saves, errors & multiplayer

Installing and updating, where worlds live, save limits, error messages, logs and the multiplayer preview.

System requirements and supported platforms

Limited

Linux with a Vulkan-capable integrated or discrete GPU and an X11 or XWayland session is the main, tested platform. Installers for Windows 10/11 (64-bit Intel/AMD) and macOS (Apple Silicon or Intel with a Metal GPU) are included but have not yet been checked with real graphics and sound on those systems.

The first build needs internet and several GB of free disk space. README says the 60 FPS target assumes at least an integrated GPU; software Vulkan (llvmpipe) is for diagnostics only (README.md:155-156).

Wiki No guide yet

Source evidence
  • Cargo.toml:50 — winit built with only the x11 feature
  • install.sh:33-38 — Linux and macOS supported by install.sh; other systems told to use install-windows.cmd
  • install-windows.ps1:18-20 — Windows installer refuses non-Windows and non-AMD64 systems
  • crates/voxelgame-render/src/loading.rs:53-68 — prefers a high-performance GPU, falls back to a software adapter

Install on Linux (install.sh)

Available

From the extracted source folder run `bash install.sh` as your normal user. It installs compiler and audio tools (apt-get, dnf or pacman, using sudo only for system packages), Rust stable, builds the game and adds Voxelgame to your application menu. Setup never starts the game or touches existing worlds.

bash install.sh [--yes] [--prefix PATH]…
Run setup; --yes accepts the plan, --prefix changes the app folder, --skip-prerequisites uses tools you installed yourself, --help changes nothing (terminal in the extracted source folder)

Needs internet, several GB free, a working Vulkan driver and X11/XWayland. Other distributions: install the prerequisites listed in docs/INSTALLING.md:69-72 yourself, then use --skip-prerequisites. Fedora gets ffmpeg-free. INSTALLING.md says not to run setup with sudo; the script does not enforce this.

Wiki Guide · Install, update and find your worlds

Install on macOS (Install-macOS.command)

Limited

Double-click Install-macOS.command, press Return to accept the plan, finish Apple's Command Line Tools installer if offered, and enter your Mac password if Homebrew asks. Setup installs Homebrew and FFmpeg when needed plus Rust, builds the game for your Mac, and creates Voxelgame.app in your home folder's Applications folder.

Unsigned source installer, not a notarized app: if macOS blocks it use System Settings > Privacy & Security > Open Anyway, or run `bash install.sh` in Terminal; do not disable Gatekeeper. Native macOS graphics and audio are untested, and an owner-supplied Metal startup fix is not yet integrated, so the game may fail to start. On some Macs F4 needs Fn+F4. The extracted folder can be deleted after a successful install.

Limited

Where the game, worlds and logs are stored

Available

Installed games keep worlds and settings in a per-user data folder that survives upgrades: Linux ~/.local/share/voxelgame/data, macOS ~/Library/Application Support/Voxelgame, Windows %LOCALAPPDATA%\Voxelgame\data. Worlds are in the worlds folder inside it. A source checkout started with./run.sh keeps its worlds in the source folder.

Worlds from a development checkout are not moved automatically; copying the worlds folder into the data folder while the game is closed is the implied manual route (inferred from relative save paths).

  • install.sh:166-167 — Linux/macOS launcher changes into the data folder first

Updating an installed game

Limited

There is no separate updater: close the game, extract the newer source folder and run its installer again. Worlds and settings stay in the data folder, a failed build leaves the old version working, and the launcher switches to the new version only after it is completely copied.

Missing today: update-existing detection, version/origin checks, a check that the game is closed, rollback and clean-up of old versions (delete them yourself after checking the new one). Going back to an older build is not supported and may fail to open worlds saved by the newer one (current save format 22). A source checkout launched with./run.sh rebuilds itself when its sources change (run.sh:76-107).

Uninstalling

Limited

There is no uninstaller. Delete the app folder and its menu entry (Linux ~/.local/share/applications/voxelgame.desktop, Windows Start menu 'Voxelgame' shortcut). Your worlds stay in the data folder until you delete it yourself.

Rust, Homebrew, compilers and audio tools stay installed. On Windows the FFmpeg copy in %LOCALAPPDATA%\Voxelgame\tools also remains. Deleting the data folder removes all worlds permanently.

Available

On a prepared Linux machine with Rust 1.75 or newer, run `cargo run --release --locked --bin voxelgame`, or `./run.sh`, which rebuilds only when sources changed and shows a small 'Preparing the game' window while it builds. Started this way, worlds live in the source folder's worlds directory.

Developer route. Optional aplay (alsa-utils) for sound and ffmpeg for music (README.md:153).

World save files

Available

Any mode

Each world is a single.vxw file inside the worlds folder. The starting world is worlds/debug/debug.vxw and is listed as DEBUG. Creating a world with a name makes worlds/<name>/world.vxw plus a name.txt label; leaving the name empty makes worlds/world-0001/world.vxw, world-0002 and so on.

There is no seed field when creating a world. Only your changes are stored; untouched terrain is regenerated from the seed.

Available

Menus

Every time the game starts, the active world is the starting world worlds/debug/debug.vxw (its name, DEBUG, is shown under the title), so Continue opens that world after a restart. To keep playing another world, open Worlds and load it.

Settings are stored per world, so the settings shown right after launch are the DEBUG world's (see per-world-settings).

Saving: autosave, F6 and quitting safely

Available

Any mode

The world saves when you press F6, choose Main menu or Save & quit in the Esc menu, press Ctrl+Q, close the window, choose Quit on the main menu, or load or create another world. Every 30 seconds autosave saves if the world changed. If saving fails while quitting, the game stays open so nothing is lost.

F6
Save now ('World saved safely') (in a world)
Ctrl+Q
Save and quit (in game)
Esc > Main menu / Save & quit
Save, then return to the main menu or close (Settings panel in a world)

Autosave is triggered by world changes such as building, mining, home storage, journal edits or boats; just walking around or most crafting waits for the next F6 or quit. There is no crash handler, so a crash loses changes since the last save, but the previous save file stays intact.

What a world save keeps

Available

Creative · Survival

A save keeps your position and view, game mode, health, hunger, thirst, stamina and temperature, inventory, quick-slot bindings and selection, equipped tool, every block you changed (with water state), time/weather/season controls, home crate and rest point, one saved build palette, journal places and expedition finds, the map destination, sailing boats and your settings. Animals, projectiles, primed TNT and Study Grove timers are not saved.

Session-only (reset on load): Performance (F3), Chunk borders (F7), LOD view (F8), the FPS and coordinates readout (on by default) and Study Grove settings/counts. Creative and survival worlds use the same format; the mode is stored.

Settings are stored inside each world

Limited

Any mode

Graphics, audio and GUI settings are saved inside each world file. A new world copies your current settings; loading another world switches to that world's own settings.

Because the game always starts on the DEBUG world, settings you changed while in another world appear again only when you load that world. An owner request to refine per-world settings restore is open.

World size limits

Available

Creative · Survival

Each world file is capped at 8 MiB and 200,000 changed half-metre blocks. From 190,000 changes the game repeats a warning ('saving stops at 200000'), and building refuses changes beyond the budget with 'Save edit budget reached'.

Older and newer saves

Available

Any mode

Worlds keep the terrain generator they were created with, so old builds and untouched land stay together; new worlds use generation 10. Worlds from before the half-metre block grid are refused ('a new world is required'), and a world saved by a newer version of the game is refused by an older one.

Error texts: 'not a voxelgame save', 'world predates the half-metre voxel grid; a new world is required', 'world was saved by a newer version of voxelgame', 'debug save exceeds the 8 MiB safety budget'.

When a world cannot be loaded

Limited

Any mode

A damaged or incompatible world file is never overwritten. If you pick it in Worlds, the menu shows 'world could not be loaded:...' and you stay where you were. If the world the game opens at startup cannot be read, the game closes and prints the reason only to a terminal.

Because startup always opens worlds/debug/debug.vxw (or VOXELGAME_SAVE_PATH), an unreadable starting world blocks the main menu; moving that file aside lets the game start with a fresh starting world. Run the launcher from a terminal to read the message.

Startup and crash error messages

Limited

Any mode

When the game cannot start, for example with no usable GPU, an unreadable starting world or a mistyped option, it closes and prints the reason to the terminal ('voxelgame failed:...' or 'voxelgame could not start:...'). Menu and desktop launches show no error window, so start the launcher from a terminal to see the message.

Other messages: 'GPU ran out of memory during startup', 'Nearby terrain took too long to prepare; please try again' (shown on the menu), 'audio disabled: playback command unavailable (aplay on Linux; ffplay on Windows/macOS)'. Problems loading other worlds are shown on the main menu instead. Only run.sh shows a dialog, and only for a failed build (run.sh:100-104). Linux launcher path for terminal use: ~/.local/share/voxelgame/app/launch.sh (install.sh:140).

Lag-spike log

Available

Any mode

While the Performance overlay (F3) is on, frames slower than twice your frame budget (at least 25 ms) are recorded with their slowest causes in lag-spikes.jsonl under ~/.local/state/voxelgame (or $XDG_STATE_HOME/voxelgame). Turn F3 off to stop recording.

Entries include world seed, position, frame cost and up to eight contributors, which makes them useful for bug reports. See data-locations for the macOS/Windows path caveats.

Graphics driver and display problems

Limited

On Linux the game needs a working Vulkan driver and an X11 or XWayland session; it has no native Wayland window. It picks your high-performance GPU and falls back automatically to a software renderer such as llvmpipe, which is fine for diagnosis but too slow for normal play.

No in-game GPU diagnostics beyond the F3 overlay. macOS needs a Metal-capable GPU; Windows graphics are not yet validated. Lowering Horizon distance, turning Distant terrain off or choosing Shader None reduces GPU load.

Sound and music requirements

Available

Any mode

Sound effects play through aplay on Linux (alsa-utils) and ffplay on Windows and macOS; music also needs ffmpeg to decode the songs. The installers set these up. Without the player program the game runs silently; without ffmpeg, Music switches itself off and the status line shows 'Music unavailable:...'.

After installing ffmpeg, switch Music back on in Settings > Audio. Song files may be mp3, ogg, wav or flac.

Join a dedicated server (--connect)

In development

Any mode

There is no Multiplayer menu yet. From a terminal you can start the game with --connect=HOST[:PORT] (port 27015 by default) and --name=NAME to join a running voxelgame-server. You see other players, can build together and chat, and the server's world is never written into your own saves.

voxelgame --connect=HOST[:PORT] --name=NAME
Join a server instead of opening a local world (command line)

Limits in this build: in survival, damage and death are not applied while connected; animals, inventories and crafting are not shared; water flow comes from the server (game.rs:1338-1340). The first server you join is trusted and pinned in known_servers.txt; a changed certificate is refused. Identity files client-certificate.der/client-key.der live in ~/.local/state/voxelgame. LAN/loopback only: the network library has known denial-of-service defects.

Run a dedicated server (voxelgame-server)

In development

The dedicated server is a separate program that the installers do not build. Built from source, `voxelgame-server --world DIR` hosts a world on 127.0.0.1:27015 by default; for LAN play bind your LAN address, for example --bind 192.168.1.20:27015. Its console accepts /list, /say, /save, /stop and /help.

/list, /say <text>, /save, /stop, /help
List players, broadcast, save now, save and stop, show commands (server console)

Other options: --seed, --name, --motd, --max-players, --autosave-minutes. Developers can test with the scripted bot: cargo run --release -p voxelgame-server --example bot -- HOST:PORT.

Headless screenshots and benchmarks (command line)

Developer tool

Advanced: `voxelgame --headless --screenshot=FILE.png` or `--headless --bench=SECONDS` renders offscreen with the normal renderer, without a window, audio or save writes, and can run beside the open game. Benchmarks print one BENCH line with mean, median, 1%-low and worst frame times.

--headless --screenshot=PATH [--screenshot-after=SECS] /…
Capture one PNG or measure frame times, then exit (command line)

Other options: --screen=world|menu|inventory|settings|map, --position=X,Y,Z, --look=YAW,PITCH, --time=cycle|dawn|day|dusk|night|0..1, --weather=..., --shader=none|fast|cinematic, --view-distance=N, --window=WxH, --uncap, --auto-start, --no-save. Works in normal builds but is a developer tool. There is no --profile flag.

02 / WRITING ORDER

The guides players need next.

Practical, task-based guides ranked by how many players need them and whether the feature is ready to document. Each guide will be checked in a disposable headless game session before it is published.

  1. Getting started: your first session Written

    New players need the start menu, the creative default, the pack, the hotbar and safe quitting before anything else.

    Covers: Start menu, Creative and survival modes (F4), New worlds: creative by default, survival starter supplies, Walking and looking around, Inventory screen and its tabs, Mouse capture and release, Saving, Main menu and quitting

  2. Controls reference Written

    One verified key table replaces the game README table, which has known mistakes.

    Covers: Walking and looking around, Jumping, Sprinting, Sneaking (ledge guard), Crawling, Swimming and diving, Creative flight, Hold to zoom, Camera perspectives (F5), Ten-slot hotbar, Equipping tools (Tab cycling)

  3. Your first survival day Written

    Survival starts with a small starter pack; players need the shortest safe path to tools, food, water and a respawn point.

    Covers: Health, hunger, thirst and stamina, Eating (R), Drinking and water flasks (T), Mining and collecting blocks, Craft tab (crafting panel), Stone tools (single tier, no durability), Home crate: establish, storage, repair, pack up, Resting and setting your respawn point

  4. Crafting and recipes Written

    All 40 recipes are verified; the guide can also warn that X may burn the starter boards and that Lumen crystal is scarce.

    Covers: Craft tab (crafting panel), Complete recipe list, Interchangeable ingredients, Quick craft (X), Charcoal, cooking and glass (no furnace), Lumen-crystal recipes in survival

  5. Maps and finding your way home Needs screenshots

    Players lose builds after travel; markers, journal places and the destination beacon already help.

    Covers: Compact map, Fullscreen world map, Map locator: find biomes and landmarks, Right-click map markers, Journal places and notes, Destinations: map marker, light beacon and on-screen marker, The map in survival (chart only, no fog of war)

  6. Install, update and where your worlds live Written

    Reinstalling is the only update path and Continue reopens the default world, so players need clear file locations.

    Covers: Install on Linux (install.sh), Install on Windows 10/11 (install-windows.cmd), Install on macOS (Install-macOS.command), Updating an installed game, Where the game, worlds and logs are stored, World save files, Which world Continue opens after a restart

  7. Building basics and creative tools Needs screenshots

    Placement, half-metre detail, brushes and undo are the core of creative play.

    Covers: Target outline and placement ghost, Placing blocks, Half-metre detail building (hold Shift), Creative brushes (B), Copy brush (copy and paste), Undo and redo building, Build tab and material palettes

  8. Sailing a boat Needs screenshots

    Wind, tacking and the helm controls are not obvious without a walkthrough.

    Covers: Launching and packing up a sailing boat, Sailing: deck, helm, sails, steering and camera, Sailing: wind, speed and tacking, Boats and saving

  9. Hunting, weapons and animals Written

    Animals never attack; hunting is the renewable food source and the bow and rifle have specific controls.

    Covers: Hitting animals (melee), Alder bow and arrows, Alder rifle and rifle rounds, Throwing rocks, Animal drops, Animal behaviour, Peaceful world: no hostile mobs

  10. Settings and performance Needs screenshots

    Shader tier, horizon and frame limit decide smoothness on laptops; measured guidance follows in the performance study.

    Covers: Shader quality: None, Fast, Cinematic, Horizon distance, Frame limit, Atmospheric fog (haze) presets, Field of view, Performance overlay (F3)

  11. Fixing startup, sound and save problems Written

    Fatal errors currently appear only in a terminal, so players need to know where logs and saves are.

    Covers: Startup and crash error messages, When a world cannot be loaded, Graphics driver and display problems, Sound and music requirements, Installer logs, Saving: autosave, F6 and quitting safely

  12. Study Grove focus timer Needs screenshots

    An owner-requested study mode with its own controls and backdrops.

    Covers: Study Grove focus timer, Study over your own world (Real terrain backdrop)

  13. Not in the game yet Waiting for the feature

    One honest page answers the common “is this in the game?” questions without inventing details.

    Covers: Fire, Lava, Natural waterfalls and dripstone caves, Doors, storage chests and furniture, Player skins and skin editor

03 / WHERE DOCUMENTS DISAGREE

The code wins.

The audit compared the game’s own README and documents with its code. Where they disagree, this ledger follows the code, and the mismatch is listed here for the game’s maintainers.

  • Seasons are not yet visual-only

    The design philosophy says seasons are visual only, but in survival the season still moves the air temperature by up to 7 °C, which can matter on the highest peaks on winter nights.

    docs/PHILOSOPHY.md:27 crates/voxelgame-core/src/environment.rs:409 crates/voxelgame-core/src/game.rs:2572

  • World list limit and folder names

    The README says the Worlds menu holds 32 worlds and that new worlds get numbered folders. The code lists up to 256 worlds, and a typed world name gets its own folder.

    README.md:661-666 src/worlds.rs:13 src/worlds.rs:208-232

  • Tab and the equipment card

    The README says Tab cycles a 3D equipment card. That card was removed; Tab still cycles carried tools and the status line names the result.

    README.md:601 crates/voxelgame-render/src/hotbar_ui.rs:342-344

  • The alder rifle needs Lumen crystal

    The README calls the rifle craftable. Its recipe needs 8 Lumen crystal pieces, and a survival world contains a single piece at one landmark, so rifles, rounds, TNT and dynamite are effectively creative-only.

    README.md:360-361 crates/voxelgame-core/src/inventory.rs:1173-1179 crates/voxelgame-core/src/game/exploration.rs:240

  • T at the water’s edge

    The README says T drinks a carried flask. Next to drinkable water, T drinks from the water and refills every empty flask instead.

    README.md:633 crates/voxelgame-core/src/game/consumables.rs:91-110

  • Multiplayer is further along than the README says

    The README says multiplayer is not playable yet. A self-built dedicated server and the --connect option already share movement, building and chat; there is no menu entry and survival damage is not applied.

    README.md:785-786 src/launch.rs:164-166 — --connect/--name options; needs a window src/launch.rs:296-303 — --connect/--name options; needs a window

04 / METHOD & LIMITS

Checked against the source.

Source, not memory

The audit read an exact export of the audited commit: input handling, menus, crafting, survival, building, world, maps, sailing, combat, platform and settings code. Every feature cites at least one file and line, and the game’s own documents were checked against that code.

Planned means absent

Tracked requests were searched for in the same export. Anything missing, or present only as code that ordinary players cannot reach, is marked Planned or In development, never Available.

Not yet a play test

This ledger records what the code supports. Practical guides add controls and screenshots verified in disposable headless sessions, never a visible game window or a normal player save.

Numbers come from the code

Capacities, ranges, timings and recipe amounts are copied from the constants that define them. When a later game change moves them, the next audit updates this page and its commit.

Audited commit dd29d912918978b9d0e74ec1104b87c0679d793e on branch main, committed 2026-10-10T22:47:55+08:00. Evidence paths and line numbers refer to that commit in the private game repository; later game changes can move them.
